design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing - close the project account out and tell me what
to pay - and the scored figure sits at the bottom of a four-problem tree whose other three problems he
never mentions and could not know about. The settlement rule itself says the figure waits on two states of
the record that do not hold at the opening: retainage standing released, and every month past due carried
as a late fee. Working out the release leads, through the release rule's own sentence, to a third problem:
the days of delay standing credited. Each of the four writes is a multi-factor calculation over the same
reconciled ledger, read at four different moments, and three of them read another product line's records.
Nothing here is tool-choice difficulty: each hidden tool is named only by the policy that computes its
parameter.

SCOPE. Occupied by this task: retrofit_ext_liquidated_damages_credit, retrofit_ext_overdue_invoice_late_fee,
retrofit_ext_retainage_release and retrofit_ext_closeout_balance_payment, with the task tools
credit_liquidated_damages_732a84c1, bill_overdue_late_fee_5c3179f3, release_project_retainage_a81bb865 and
pay_project_balance_ec87bb4f, over the subjects retrofit_credit_issued, retrofit_progress_billed (late fee
class), retrofit_retainage_released and retrofit_payment_received. Occupied earlier by task 0:
retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing and retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement with bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e
and settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f, over retrofit_progress_billed (storage class) and
retrofit_project_cancelled. The two tasks share no policy, no tool and no computed quantity; they meet only
in the base policies they both inherit, which is common knowledge and not a claim. Nothing is reserved for
later: this difficulty is M = 2 and the two scopes together cover all six extended policies.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/retrofit_projects_desk
--task 1): {"task": 1, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/retrofit_projects_desk/1",
"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 6, 6]}. The tree therefore has exactly
three prerequisite problems, and the four computations carry 5, 4, 6 and 6 declared factors: the closing
payment takes 5, the retainage release 4, the liquidated damages 6 and the late fee 6.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root problem: retrofit_ext_closeout_balance_payment (payment_amount_usd, owner=user tool
    pay_project_balance_ec87bb4f - the money leaves the owner's account on his own authority).
  prerequisite problems: retrofit_ext_retainage_release (retainage_release_usd, agent),
    retrofit_ext_overdue_invoice_late_fee (late_fee_amount_usd, agent) and
    retrofit_ext_liquidated_damages_credit (damages_credit_usd, agent).
  edge payment <- retainage release: kind value_input; gate = the payment's compute binding
    retainage_released_total; form state; prerequisite sentence, verbatim in the payment policy's own rule:
    "The amount an owner settles a project at is fixed only after the retainage held on the project stands
    released on its account."; handling-time condition: the retainage held on the project stands released on
    its account; resolved by release_project_retainage_a81bb865 (agent).
  edge payment <- late fee: kind value_input; gate = the payment's compute binding late_fees_total; form
    state; prerequisite sentence: "Before the amount to settle is worked out, every month the project's
    billings have stood past their due day must be carried as a late fee on the project's billing record.";
    condition: every month past due is carried as a late fee on the billing record; resolved by
    bill_overdue_late_fee_5c3179f3 (agent).
  edge retainage release <- liquidated damages: kind value_input; gate = the release's compute binding
    credits_on_project; form state; prerequisite sentence, verbatim in the release policy's own rule: "The
    retainage released on a project is worked out only after every day of delay past the day substantial
    completion was guaranteed by stands credited on the project's account."; condition: every day of delay
    past the guaranteed day stands as a credit on the project's account; resolved by
    credit_liquidated_damages_732a84c1 (agent).
  FOUR-POINT TEST, applied to each sentence. (1) Ordering connective: "only after" in the first and third,
    "Before ... must" in the second, each joining that policy's own result to what it waits on. (2) The
    waited-on side is a record-visible state in all three - retainage standing released on the account, a
    late fee carried on the billing record, a credit standing on the account - and none of them names an
    action, a performer or a tool. (3) None carries a tool name, a policy id, a snake_case token or a row
    id. (4) Each is written at exactly the strength and scope of its edge: a hard "only after" or "must",
    over the retainage held, over every month past due, over every day of delay, no wider and no narrower
    than the condition recorded on the edge. THE STATE FORM WAS AVAILABLE IN ALL THREE and is used; for each,
    exactly one write of this difficulty brings the state about - only the retainage release rule books a
    release, only the late fee rule books a late fee, only the liquidated damages rule books a credit for
    days of delay - so each hop resolves uniquely. The derivations: (a) sentence -> the account shows
    retainage of 61586.00 standing held and nothing released -> the only rule that books a release is the
    retainage release rule -> release the retainage first; (b) sentence -> the billing record shows progress
    billings due since 2026-01-31 and no late fee line at all -> the only rule that books a late fee is the
    late fee rule -> raise it first; (c) sentence -> the account carries no credit while the system was
    accepted on 2026-04-03 against a guaranteed day the record puts at 2026-02-07 -> the only rule that
    books a credit for days of delay is the liquidated damages rule -> credit them first.
  WHY EACH IS FALSE AT frozen_time. Retainage: initial_state.retrofit_events holds three
    retrofit_retainage_withheld rows (18550.00, 24486.00, 18550.00) and not one retrofit_retainage_released
    row, and retrofit_projects.retainage_held_usd stands at 61586.00. Late fee: every retrofit_progress_billed
    row on the project is a deposit, a mobilisation, a progress or a remobilisation line, and none has
    billing_class late_fee, although the most recent progress billing fell due on 2026-01-31 and only
    15000.00 has been paid against it. Credit: there is no retrofit_credit_issued row on the project at all.
  LOAD-BEARING (Step 5 prerequisite-sensitivity run, figures reproduced by check_compute --task 1). Skipping
    the liquidated damages credit leaves the release at 39748.50 instead of 5998.50. Skipping the retainage
    release leaves the payment at 139083.34 instead of 128315.60. Skipping the late fee leaves the payment at
    122956.52 instead of 128315.60.
  TOPOLOGICAL ORDER: liquidated damages, late fee, retainage release, closing payment - the gold write nodes
    at actions 10, 12, 14 and 16 in that order. PARALLEL EDGES: the late fee problem is a sibling of the
    release-and-damages chain, so the pair may be taken in either order. They commute, and the run proves it:
    the late fee computation reads the deposit, mobilisation, progress and change order billings, the
    retainage withheld, the payments and the due dates, and touches neither credits nor releases; the release
    computation reads the withholdings, the progress billings, the payments, the inspections and the credits,
    and its unpaid measure is defined to exclude late fees and remobilisation fees expressly, so a late fee
    raised before or after it changes nothing. All three legal orders were run - damages, late fee, release;
    damages, release, late fee; and late fee, damages, release - and each gives 33750.00, 5413.22, 5998.50
    and 128315.60 with the same terminal rows, field for field.
  NO USER HINT: user_scenario never names a prerequisite problem, never mentions retainage, a late fee, a
    credit, damages, lateness or anything owed beyond what his own ledger shows, and never suggests an order
    of work. He asks to close the account out and pay. His one line about the office side - "he is happy for
    the desk to put whatever the contract requires onto the account on its own side before it gives him a
    figure" - names nothing, and his cooperative line fires only after the agent has itself said something
    must go onto the account.
  TOOLS DO NOT BLOCK: pay_project_balance_ec87bb4f in task_tools.py looks the project row up, writes the
    payment row and updates the balance; it reads no retainage, no credit and no billing class, and returns
    no policy-based refusal, so it writes faithfully with none of the three prerequisites resolved.
    release_project_retainage_a81bb865 likewise never looks for a credit, and bill_overdue_late_fee_5c3179f3
    and credit_liquidated_damages_732a84c1 check nothing at all. The whole consequence of skipping a
    prerequisite is a terminal hash that differs from gold.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1, subject retrofit_credit_issued. The only base policy whose subject covers it is
  retrofit_schedule_guarantee. Its one gate, completion_past_guaranteed_date, is a time gate whose condition
  is the very sentence this task's policy supersedes (the guarantee counted from mobilisation and extended by
  every issued change order), so the gate is retired by that declared overwrite and the policy governs by its
  scope alone; base's amount sentence (the tier's daily amount for each calendar day past that date, capped at the tier's portion of the contract value) is likewise declared superseded, replaced by the extended damages sentence, so that the additions to the daily amount and the grace and suspension days are a declared version update and not a second reading; the extended rule replaces it with a guaranteed period whose anchor, extension, grace and
  suspension are each decided from the record. The semantic boundary the retired gate used to draw is still
  drawn, and by hand: the system was accepted on 2026-04-03, and the guaranteed period as this policy counts
  it ends 227 days after the booked day of 2025-08-04 (180 guaranteed, 12 extended, 5 of grace, 30 of
  suspension), that is on 2026-03-19, so the project is late and damages are owed; had it been accepted on or
  before 2026-03-19 the delay would have counted as none and no credit would be written at all.
  Write 2, subject retrofit_progress_billed. Governed by retrofit_progress_billing_and_retainage alone; its
  only gate applies to retrofit_retainage_released and so does not reach a billing, which is governed by that
  policy's scope. No time gate.
  Write 3, subject retrofit_retainage_released. Governed by retrofit_progress_billing_and_retainage, whose
  gate retainage_release_after_completion DOES apply and is inherited whole: retainage is released within the
  class's release period counted forward in calendar days from the day the system was accepted as running for
  its intended use, provided the punch list is cleared and the closeout documents are delivered. Anchor:
  retrofit_projects.substantial_completion_date = 2026-04-03, copied verbatim from the base temporal_basis.
  Duration: variants.retainage_release_days = 60 for this class. Direction: not_after, boundary inclusive.
  2026-04-03 plus 60 calendar days is 2026-06-02, and frozen_time is 2026-05-06, so the release is inside the
  window; at 2026-06-02 it would still be inside, and at 2026-06-03 it would be out and the release would have
  to wait on a fresh instruction rather than be written. The two provisos hold on the record: the punch list
  was cleared by the owner walkthrough passed on 2026-04-28, on or before the punch list due day of
  2026-05-01, and the closeout acceptance was confirmed on 2026-04-29.
  Write 4, subject retrofit_payment_received. Governed by retrofit_progress_billing_and_retainage; no gate of
  it applies to a payment, so its scope governs. The payment-application clause of that policy is superseded
  clause by clause on the extended side, because this policy settles the account as a whole rather than the
  oldest invoice first.
  AUTOMATIC CLAUSES CHECKED AGAINST THE SEED. The work-stoppage clause has already discharged: the first
  progress billing fell due 2025-11-14 and was paid 2025-12-20, 36 days past due against a 30-day stoppage
  period, so work stopped and the remobilisation fee of 9500.00 was raised when it resumed - which is exactly
  the row the guarantee-suspension factor reads. Nothing further falls out of it, the project having reached
  substantial completion. The late fee clause is the subject of this task's own late fee write and is
  discharged by it. The retainage clause is discharged by the release write. The maintenance agreement seeded
  at the building is active with its next visit due 2026-06-16, after frozen_time, and owes nothing today;
  the service program and the energy subscription are read only and owe nothing today either.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is project 13a88bb2 (Turnkey Mechanical Upgrade Project, central

Included in the contract billings: the deposit 148400.00, the mobilisation fee 8500.00 and the three progress

rules: the remobilisation fee 9500.00 and any late fee. Included in the withholdings: 18550.00, 24486.00 and
18550.00 against the three progress invoices they name. Included in the payments: 148400.00, 8500.00,
166950.00, 198114.00 and the part payment 15000.00. The two change orders are correlated to their own

WORLD ROWS AND WHAT EACH CARRIES. The booked start 2025-08-04 against the mobilisation day 2025-08-11 and the
absence of any schedule request is what moves the guarantee clock back to the booked day; delete the booked
start or add a confirmed schedule request and the delay falls from 15 days to 8. The two change orders are the
allocation trap: 12 concealed-condition days count and 9 supplier-substitution days do not, and an agent that
adds both reaches 21 and a delay of 6. The owner walkthrough of 2026-04-28 against the punch list due day of
2026-05-01 and the confirmed closeout acceptance of 2026-04-29 are the two conditions of the grace tier; drop
the acceptance and the grace falls to 2 days. The remobilisation billing is what suspends the guarantee for 30
days, and it is also the near-miss for the closing payment, since it falls due 2026-05-20 and must not be
settled now. The over-withholding of 24486.00 on a 222600.00 progress billing - 11 per cent where the class
takes 10 - is the reconciliation trap of the release: an agent that trusts retainage_held_usd releases from
61586.00 and lands 2003.40 too high. The absence of any commissioning inspection against the two authority
inspections that were passed is what puts the release share at 90 per cent. The part payment of 15000.00 on
2026-03-05 is the anchor trap of the late fee: it restarts the overdue clock at 62 days where the billing's own
due day would give 95, and it also fixes the ceiling tier. The maintenance agreement's unpaid 4820.00 and its
signature date of 2023-06-14 carry the late fee surcharge and the portfolio allowance; the service program's
2-hour critical response and clear balance carry the daily addition and the late fee rate; the energy
subscription's class carries the measured performance addition. No cache is used as a trap: balance_due
161450.00 is exactly the sum of the project balance deltas (760000.00 billed less 61586.00 withheld less
536964.00 paid), retainage_held_usd 61586.00 is exactly the sum of the withholding rows - which is precisely
why the rate check has to be done against the billings rather than against the field - and
change_allowance_remaining 0.00 is the 51940.00 credited at award less the two change orders of 34800.00 and
17140.00.

PERSONA DESIGN. Desmond Iyer is a finance-side facilities director closing a quarter: brisk, precise about
his own affairs, incurious about the contractor's. He volunteers the company and the office number, holds the
account number and the tax digits until asked, and can answer only what a payer can answer - how the money
goes, the purchase order, whether his office returned the closeout paperwork, what his ledger shows. His
conditional behaviour is woven in: he cooperates about the account only after the agent says something must go
onto it, he reads the figure back and remarks it is not what his ledger had without disputing it, and he
insists on making the payment himself because nobody else has authority over the wire. His last reaction
answers the last gold action - the payment recorded - and asks for nothing beyond it. He never states a figure
the world does not already carry, and never states any scored answer.

THE PRESCRIBED SOLUTION. Locate and verify the account, read the building, the project, the whole project
record, the lodged requests, the maintenance agreement, the service program and the energy subscription. From
the settlement rule, see that the figure waits on retainage standing released and on late fees carried, and
that neither holds; from the release rule, see that the release waits on the days of delay standing credited,
and that no credit stands. So: credit the damages first - 242 days from the booked day to acceptance, less 180
guaranteed, less 12 owner-side impact days, less 5 days of grace, less 30 days of suspension, is 15 days at
1200 + 450 + 600 a day, 33750.00, under the 37100.00 ceiling. Then the late fee - 151950.00 taken on, 62 days
from the part payment, 3 months, 1.25 at three quarters plus 0.25, that is 1.1875 per cent a month, 5413.22,
under the 7597.50 ceiling. Then the release - 59360.00 held once the over-withholding is corrected, less
15195.00 for the unpaid work, 44165.00 releasable, 90 per cent of it 39748.50, less the whole 33750.00 credit,
5998.50. Then hand the payment over - 750500.00 of billings already due, less 61586.00 withheld, plus the
5998.50 released, plus the 5413.22 of late fee, less 536964.00 paid, less the whole of the credits at 33750.00, is
129611.72, less the 1 per cent portfolio allowance of 1296.12, is 128315.60, paid by wire.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Running the guarantee from mobilisation (8 days of delay) -
excluded by the anchor rule, which moves it to the booked day when the crew started late with no schedule
request on file. Adding the supplier's 9 impact days - excluded by the allocation rule. Missing the 30 days of
suspension - excluded by the remobilisation fee standing on the record. Taking the retainage held from the
project field - excluded by the rate check against the progress billings. Releasing the whole of it - excluded
by the unpaid-work retention and by the missing commissioning inspection. Running the overdue clock from the
invoice due day (95 days, 4 months) - excluded by the anchor rule, which restarts it on the part payment.
Settling the remobilisation fee that is not yet due - excluded by the due-now rule while retainage still stands
held. Taking only half the credit off the settlement - excluded by the credit rule, which takes the whole of it off once
retainage on the project has been released, half being taken off only while none has been. Paying before the three writes land
- excluded by the two prerequisite sentences the settlement rule carries: skipping the release drops the figure to
139083.34 and skipping the late fee drops it to 122956.52.

RULE <-> COMPUTE SWEEP. Forward: compute_basis quotes a rule sentence verbatim for every binding of all four
policies that reads the world or chooses - the anchor, extension, grace and suspension ladders and the two
cross-product daily-amount ladders on the damages; the fee base, clock anchor, month count, rate, surcharge and
ceiling ladders on the late fee; the rate check, unpaid retention, inspection share and credit offset ladders on
the release; and the due-now, released-retainage, credit, late fee and allowance ladders on the payment - as
well as the aggregates, the caps and the roundings. Reverse: every load-bearing sentence of all four rules is
claimed by a binding. The counting conventions are pinned in prose and implemented as written: "the last day of
the period excluded and the day of acceptance included" by DAYS between the anchor and the acceptance day less
the guaranteed days; "each month or part month begun counts as a whole month" by int((days + 29) / 30) against
"only the whole months completed count" by int(days / 30); "where the days of delay fall below zero they are
counted as none" by MX(0, ...); "the smaller of the two" by MN; every "rounded to the nearest cent" by RND(...,
2). The acting bases are pinned too: the damages ceiling acts on the contract value and not on the damages; the
release share acts on the releasable retainage and the credits come off after it; the late fee acts on the
amount the fee is taken on and its ceiling on the same amount; and on the payment the portfolio allowance acts
on the figure after the additions and deductions, with one rounding at the end.

FACTOR CARD.
  guarantee_clock_anchor (method, damages): ladder mobilisation day / schedule-request day / booked day. Tier
    taken: the third - mobilisation 2025-08-11 is after the booked start 2025-08-04 and no confirmed schedule
    request stands. Evidence: retrofit_projects.scheduled_start_date and .mobilization_date, and the absence of
    a schedule_request row. Baseline: the mobilisation day, which gives 18000.00.
  change_impact_allocation (method, damages): ladder every impact day (a change the owner asked for) / the
    concealed-condition and code-requirement days alone / half the supplier's days rounded down. Tier taken: the
    second - CO-10331 states 12 days on a concealed condition, CO-10402 states 9 on a supplier substitution, and
    no change order is owner-requested or an acceleration. Baseline: no extension, which gives 37100.00 at the ceiling.
  closeout_grace_allowance (parameter, damages, multi-source): ladder 5 days / 2 days / none. Tier taken: the
    first - the walkthrough of 2026-04-28 is on or before the punch list due day of 2026-05-01 and the closeout
    acceptance of 2026-04-29 stands confirmed. Baseline: no grace, which gives 37100.00.
  arrears_guarantee_suspension (parameter, damages): ladder the class's stoppage period / half of it / none.
    Tier taken: the first - a remobilisation fee stands billed. Baseline: no suspension, which gives 37100.00.
  performance_daily_amount (parameter, damages, cross-difficulty on energy): ladder the class's daily amount
    plus the performance addition / plus the metering addition / the daily amount alone. Tier taken: the first -
    the Measurement & Verification Program covering the building carries a guaranteed savings commitment.
    Baseline: the class's daily amount alone, which gives 27000.00.
  critical_response_addition (parameter, damages, cross-difficulty on service): ladder the critical addition /
    the standard addition / none. Tier taken: the first - the Critical Facility Response Program stands active
    and guarantees 2 hours at a critical facility. Baseline: no addition, which gives 24750.00.
  overdue_base_scope (method, late fee): ladder net of retainage / progress billings alone / everything billed
    less payments. Tier taken: the first - substantially complete with retainage withheld. Baseline: everything
    billed less payments, which gives 7607.22.
  overdue_clock_anchor (method, late fee): ladder the last payment / the last progress due day / no clock. Tier
    taken: the first - the part payment of 2026-03-05 came after the due day of 2026-01-31. Baseline: the due
    day, which gives 7217.62.
  overdue_month_count (method, late fee): ladder part months count whole / pro rata by the day / one month. Tier
    taken: the first - 62 days is 60 or more. Baseline: one month, which gives 1804.41.
  account_standing_rate (parameter, late fee, cross-difficulty on service, multi-source): ladder half / three
    quarters / the full rate. Tier taken: the second - the service program stands active and clear while the fee
    base is more than a tenth of the contract value. Baseline: the full rate, which gives 6837.75.
  portfolio_arrears_surcharge (parameter, late fee, cross-difficulty on maintenance, multi-source): ladder the
    arrears surcharge / the mild surcharge / none. Tier taken: the second - the maintenance agreement stands
    active and carries 4820.00 unpaid. Baseline: no surcharge, which gives 4273.59.
  payment_silence_ceiling (parameter, late fee): ladder 10 / 5 / 2 per cent. Tier taken: the second - 62 days
    since the last payment. Baseline: 2 per cent, which gives 3039.00 at the ceiling.
  withholding_rate_check (method, release): ladder recompute at the class's rate / the recorded sum / nothing
    held. Tier taken: the first - 24486.00 was withheld from a 222600.00 billing. Baseline: the recorded sum,
    which gives 8001.90.
  unpaid_work_retention (method, release, multi-source): ladder hold back the rate on the unpaid amount / the
    whole held amount / nothing. Tier taken: the first - 151950.00 stands unpaid. Baseline: the whole held
    amount, which gives 19674.00.
  inspection_release_share (parameter, release, multi-source): ladder the whole / 90 per cent / 50 per cent.
    Tier taken: the second - two authority inspections passed and no commissioning inspection. Baseline: the
    whole, which gives 10415.00.
  credit_offset_on_release (parameter, release, multi-source): ladder the whole of the credits / half / none.
    Tier taken: the first - the unpaid amount is more than a tenth of the contract value. Baseline: none, which
    gives 39748.50.
  due_now_scope (method, payment): ladder billings already due / progress billings already due / every billing.
    Tier taken: the first - the project stands substantially complete and has not been closed out, so the
    remobilisation fee falling due 2026-05-20 is left to its own term. Baseline: every billing raised, which
    gives 137720.60.
  released_retainage_settlement (parameter, payment): ladder the whole / half / none. Tier taken: the first -
    the class allows 60 days for the release. Baseline: none, which gives 122377.09.
  credit_settlement_share (parameter, payment, multi-source): ladder the whole / half / none. Tier taken: the
    first - credits stand on the project and retainage held on it has been released. Baseline: half, the rest
    waiting on a release, which gives 145021.85.
  arrears_late_fee_settlement (parameter, payment): ladder every late fee / half / none. Tier taken: the first -
    the unpaid amount is more than a fifth of the contract value. Baseline: none, which gives 122956.52.
  portfolio_settlement_allowance (parameter, payment, cross-difficulty on maintenance, multi-source): ladder 1
    per cent / half of 1 per cent / none. Tier taken: the first - an active agreement signed 2023-06-14, before
    the award of 2025-04-22. Baseline: none, which gives 129611.72.
  An agent who reads only the four computation documents and none of the twenty-one factor documents computes
  37100.00, 2669.20, 61586.00 and 144575.00: four definite, wrong numbers. No factor's tier is read off a stamp;
  in particular retainage_held_usd is present and exactly equal to the recorded withholdings, and the release
  rule deliberately reads the billings instead.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this
dossier, and working only from the prose the four rules will publish, the tool schemas, what the finders return
and what Desmond actually says: the request selects settling one project account; the settlement rule is the

user_scenario:
Desmond Iyer looks after the buildings and the building money for Calloway Ridge Medical Holdings, and he rings the client services desk mid-morning with a spreadsheet open and a quarter to close. He opens with the company, Calloway Ridge Medical Holdings, and the office number, 3125550523, and says he is the one who signs the cheques on the plant work. If the desk wants proof of who he is he reads the account number from the corner of the last invoice, 650377, and if a second detail is wanted he gives the last four digits of the federal tax identification number, 5546. Neither comes out unless he is asked, and he has never seen an internal reference number in his life.

His errand is one thing. The central plant rebuild at the medical centre is done and signed off, his engineers walked it in April and he put the acceptance through at the end of that month, and he now wants the project account settled: what is due on it now, all told, and he will pay that today rather than carry it into the next quarter. He is happy for the desk to put whatever the contract requires onto the account on its own side before it gives him a figure, but the money leaves his hands, not theirs: he will make the payment himself out of the treasury portal, because nobody else at Calloway Ridge has authority over an outgoing wire of that size, and he says so early and plainly.

He answers what a paying customer can answer. Asked how the money will be sent, he says by wire, same day. Asked for the purchase order the project sits under, he reads out PO-2025-1188. Asked whether the closeout paperwork was returned, he says yes, his office accepted it in writing at the end of April. Asked what his own ledger shows, he says accounts payable has just over a hundred and sixty-one thousand sitting against the project, though he adds that his ledger is only as good as the invoices that reached it. Asked about anything on the contractor's side of the fence, such as what has been withheld, what has been raised or how anything was worked out, he says that is exactly why he is ringing and the desk will have to tell him.

He is unhurried but he does not chat. If the agent tells him something has to be put onto the project account before a closing figure can be given, he says to go ahead and do it properly, he would rather see one clean number than three. When the agent gives him the figure he reads it back, remarks that it is not what his own ledger had, says he is not going to quarrel with it if the contract says so, and asks to be put in a position to pay it. When the agent hands the payment across to him he runs it himself and confirms the wire has gone. Once he hears the payment is recorded he thanks the desk, says that closes his quarter, and rings off.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Two of the three prerequisites sit on one chain - the damages credit before the retainage release before the payment - and the late fee is parallel to that chain, so the only freedom is where the late fee is taken. All three legal orders were actually run on this world: damages, late fee, release; damages, release, late fee; and late fee, damages, release. Each gives 33750.00, 5413.22, 5998.50 and 128315.60, and each ends in the same terminal rows, field for field, so the terminal state is unambiguous however the parallel pair is taken. The reason is in the rules themselves: the late fee computation reads the deposit, mobilisation, progress and change order billings, the retainage withheld, the payments and the due dates, and touches no credit and no release; the release computation reads the withholdings, the progress billings, the payments, the inspections and the credits, and its unpaid measure is defined in its own rule to exclude late fees and remobilisation fees expressly. The payment is last on every order, because both of its own prerequisite sentences wait on states the other writes bring about.
